newsitem.title: UK: Gehe raises bid for UK's Lloyds Chemists.
newsitem.headline: Gehe raises bid for UK's Lloyds Chemists.

text.p: German pharmaceutical wholesaler Gehe AG said on Friday it raised its cash offer for British pharmacy chain Lloyds Chemists Plc to 525 pence per ordinary share from 500 pence.
The increased offer -- which Gehe said was final -- valued Lloyds' ordinary and preference share capital at about 684.1 million pounds ($1.16 billion).

Gehe, locked in a long-running battle with rival bidder Unichem Plc for Lloyds, said the increased ordinary share offer represented a multiple of 22 times Lloyds' earnings per share for the year ended June 30, 1996.

"It has been almost a year since the original bids for Lloyds Chemists were announced. During that period there have been significant adverse developments," Gehe chairman Dieter Kammerer said in a statement.

"We do not believe that the continuing uncertainty is in the best interests of Lloyds Chemists, and we have therefore decided to increase our offers with a view to bringing this matter to a conclusion," he added.

Earlier this week, Lloyds, which had yet to act on either Gehe's or Unichem's offers, said pressures from the bid process had hurt group profits. Both bidders had until January 17 to raise their offers. Lloyds Chemists shares rose 14 pence to 526.5 by 1015 GMT, while Unichem stayed unchanged at 246 pence per share. ($1=.5922 Pound)
